$comment: Generated by node contract/tools/generate.mjs. Edit contract/tools, not these files.
notes: review: the record is input.approvals when it is not null, otherwise the record holding every launch value of heldText, otherwise {"schema":1,"seededFrom":"none"}. offeredText descends from heldText: its lineage starts with the held hash.

review lists each offered launch value that is not accepted without asking, in this order: per machine its systems then its identityFile, then the repository, then local. kind is changed when the record holds a value at that path, new otherwise.

effective lists one entry per offered system, then one identityFile entry per machine, then the repository, then local. state is offered, approved, not-driven (systems), none (identityFile, local) or built-in (repository). agent and grammar are set only for a system that runs; text holds the identityFile, the repository or local.agent, and is null for the built-in repository and for local's default path.
A value that is accepted but cannot run (approvable false) falls back to the record at the same location, and only to a recorded value that can run itself.

restrictedRefused is what agent 3.1.0 answers a restricted config set of offeredText over heldText: true exactly when heldText is not null and a launch value would wait for review against heldText's own values.

review.name: display-and-routing-only
review.purpose: A rename, a new route, another host and port, sites and a wake helper: none of it is a launch value, so it applies with no prompt and the new route is dialled.

review.name: agent-changed
review.purpose: A descendant that replaces the launcher with sh -c id. The document is still applied; this device keeps running the approved launcher and shows the new one for review, and a restricted key cannot publish it.

review.name: verb-appended-to-launcher
review.purpose: The approved launcher with self-update --rollback appended. The command is appended to the argv, so every request would run a rollback first: a launch change like any other.

review.name: shell-posix-to-powershell
review.purpose: The same argv under another shell is another command line: the grammar is part of the tuple.

review.name: restricted-cleared
review.purpose: Clearing restricted moves the pi from the dispatcher grammar to posix, so its line would be read by a shell: reviewed, and the approved dispatch tuple keeps running.

review.name: restricted-absent-equals-false
review.purpose: restricted false and no restricted give the same grammar, so dropping the key changes nothing that runs.

review.name: platform-linux-to-windows-shell-null
review.purpose: With no shell, the platform decides the grammar: linux is posix and windows is cmd, so this is a change.

review.name: platform-absent-equals-linux
review.purpose: Without a shell, linux and no platform are both posix: no change.

review.name: windows-shell-null-to-cmd
review.purpose: An editor that writes shell cmd where it was absent on Windows changes nothing that runs, so nobody is asked.

review.name: launcher-migration-posix
review.purpose: The migration every 3.1 upgrade makes: agent/src/index.mjs to bin/launcher.mjs under the same base and interpreter. Accepted without asking.

review.name: launcher-migration-windows-mixed-separators
review.purpose: The desktop writes the new launcher path with forward slashes into a backslashed Windows base; paths are compared after replacing \ with /.

review.name: migration-with-new-interpreter
review.purpose: A migration that also changes the interpreter is two changes: reviewed.

review.name: migration-with-grammar-change
review.purpose: A migration that also changes the shell changes the grammar: reviewed.

review.name: launcher-back-to-entry
review.purpose: The reverse of the migration is not a migration: a launcher replaced by a direct entry is reviewed.

review.name: migration-with-dotdot-base
review.purpose: A base with a .. segment can name another directory than it seems to: never accepted as a migration.

review.name: agent-removed
review.purpose: A system without an agent runs nothing, so removing one needs no approval; the system is simply not driven.

review.name: agent-emptied
review.purpose: An empty agent is the same as none.

review.name: machine-id-renamed-reusing-tuple
review.purpose: A value approved anywhere is accepted anywhere: renaming the tower to studio keeps both its tuples without a prompt.

review.name: new-machine-reusing-launcher
review.purpose: A new machine whose system uses a tuple already approved elsewhere is driven at once.

review.name: new-machine-new-launcher
review.purpose: A new machine with a launcher nobody approved: reviewed as new, and not driven until it is approved. No ssh process is started for it.

review.name: migration-accepted-at-another-location
review.purpose: The launcher migration of an approved tuple is accepted on a new machine as well: acceptance is by value, not by place.

review.name: identity-file-added
review.purpose: A shared identityFile chooses which private key this device uses: a launch value, reviewed as new.

review.name: identity-file-removed
review.purpose: Removing a shared identityFile needs no approval: the device falls back to its own bindings and default key.

review.name: identity-file-changed
review.purpose: Another key path where an approved one was: the approved path keeps being used until a person decides.

review.name: identity-file-invisible-character
review.purpose: An identityFile with a zero-width space looks like an approved path and is not one: it can only be reverted or left.

review.name: repo-changed
review.purpose: Another update repository is another source of this device's own updates. Signatures stop a forged build, not a frozen or redirected source, so it waits (T6).

review.name: repo-explicit-default
review.purpose: Writing the built-in repository explicitly is the same as not writing it.

review.name: repo-removed
review.purpose: Removing the repository goes back to the built-in one, which needs no approval.

review.name: local-agent-changed
review.purpose: The deprecated local block makes a Mac run node with this path on itself: another path waits.

review.name: local-default-path
review.purpose: A local block without an agent means the default path, which is accepted without asking.

review.name: local-disabled
review.purpose: A local block with enabled false is no local agent, whatever path it names.

review.name: local-agent-bidi-control
review.purpose: A local agent path holding a right-to-left override cannot be shown faithfully, so it cannot be approved.

review.name: unicode-path-not-normalised
review.purpose: é written precomposed and é written as e plus a combining accent look the same and are different paths: strings are compared by code point, with no Unicode normalisation.

review.name: argv-with-bidi-control
review.purpose: A right-to-left override makes an argv item display as something else. Not approvable: only Revert and Not now are offered, and the approved tuple keeps running.

review.name: restricted-three-element-agent
review.purpose: A restricted system with three argv items has no grammar at all (refused:restricted-agent-shape): not approvable, and the approved dispatch tuple keeps running.

review.name: held-refused-grammar-reused
review.purpose: A refused tuple the machine already holds is accepted when it is published again, so a restricted key can still rename around it; it is not runnable, so the system stays not driven.

review.name: fallback-to-location-record
review.purpose: This device approved a different launcher at tower/linux than the machine holds. The offered one waits, and the device keeps running what it approved at that location; values approved nowhere are not driven.

review.name: first-enrolment
review.purpose: A device that holds nothing and approved nothing: every launch value is new, nothing is driven until the enrolment summary is confirmed, and with nothing held a restricted push is not refused.

migration.name: migration-posix
migration.purpose: The direct entry replaced by the stable launcher under the same base.

migration.name: migration-windows-mixed-separators
migration.purpose: Separators are compared after replacing \ with /, because the desktop mixes them.

migration.name: migration-dispatch
migration.purpose: A restricted system migrates the same way.

migration.name: migration-reverse
migration.purpose: Back from the launcher to the entry is never a migration.

migration.name: migration-different-grammar
migration.purpose: The grammar must be the same.

migration.name: migration-dotdot-base
migration.purpose: A base with a .. segment is refused.

migration.name: migration-empty-prefix
migration.purpose: An empty base would make /bin/launcher.mjs at the root of the file system acceptable.

migration.name: migration-different-bases
migration.purpose: The launcher must be under the same base as the entry it replaces.

migration.name: migration-different-lengths
migration.purpose: An item added is not a migration.

migration.name: migration-same-tuple
migration.purpose: Equal tuples are accepted as equal, not as a migration: exactly one item must differ.

migration.name: migration-inert
migration.purpose: An inert tuple is never a migration of anything.
